item.title: New youth cyberviolence prevention funding added to Anti-Racism Grants
item.description:
New youth cyberviolence prevention funding added to Anti-Racism Grants jenniferdhogan Thu, 09/17/2026 - 14:15

Young people, individuals and organizations can apply for new funding through the Anti-Racism Youth Cyberviolence Prevention Grants to support projects that prevent and address cyberbullying and other forms of cyberviolence. 

The grant will help advance the Provincial Youth Cyberviolence Prevention Strategy by funding community-based and youth-centered projects that create safer, more inclusive online spaces for young people in PEI. It will also help promote anti-racism, build digital skills, and reduce barriers. 

“Government is pleased to support community-led initiatives that help prevent cyberviolence and promote anti-racism. We hope that this funding will assist young people to build the skills, knowledge, and connections they need to create safer and more inclusive online communities.”       

- Premier Rob Lantz

Funding is available through three streams:

  1. Youth and individual applicants can apply for amounts up to $2,500
  2. Communities, organizations, and charities can apply for amounts up to $5,000
  3. Larger community projects by organizations can apply for amounts up to $25,000

“We live in a time of fast-moving technology, and it’s important to draw on community knowledge and expertise to better address cyberbullying and other forms of cyberviolence,” said Minister of Justice and Public Safety Bloyce Thompson. “When we connect these projects with work underway across government, we are taking meaningful action to protect Island youth.” 

Eligible projects must align with one or more of the following goals, among others: 

  • Delivering workshops, presentations, and training on cyberviolence prevention, digital and media literacy, online safety and discriminatory online risks
  • Leading youth engagement initiatives, including youth leadership, peer education, mentorship, advocacy or projects that amplify youth voice and participation
  • Building community and organizational capacity to prevent and respond to cyberviolence through training and more
  • Developing culturally appropriate and privacy protective approaches to understand and measure marginalized youth’s online safety experiences

Applications will be accepted until 11:59 p.m. on October 30, 2026. 

For more information about the grant and to apply, visit Anti-Racism Youth Cyberviolence Prevention Grant.

item.title: Summerside and Province provide update on Sunbank monitoring
item.description:
Summerside and Province provide update on Sunbank monitoring jenniferdhogan Thu, 09/17/2026 - 13:17

The City of Summerside and the Government of Prince Edward Island continue to work together to monitor conditions following the battery fire at the Sunbank site. 

The situation remains stable. Air quality monitoring conducted in the community and reviewed by public health officials continues to indicate there is no evidence of a health risk to residents from the fire. Testing of Summerside's drinking water has also been completed and confirms the water is safe to drink.

The Chief Public Health Office has recommended that air quality monitoring continue at the site and, out of an abundance of caution, that additional air quality testing be conducted around the established monitoring perimeter.

The City of Summerside continues to lead response and environmental monitoring efforts, with support from the Chief Public Health Office, the Department of Land and Environment, emergency management partners and independent technical experts.

"I have reviewed the air quality monitoring results from last week and have continued to monitor the information as it becomes available. Based on the results to date, residents of Summerside should feel confident in the quality of both the air and drinking water and can continue their normal day-to-day activities. We will continue to support the City and environmental experts as longer-term monitoring plans for air, soil and water are developed and implemented."

- Chief Public Health Officer Dr. Heather Morrison

While conditions at the site have stabilized, the Summerside Fire Department continues to actively monitor the scene. Battery fires can take longer to fully extinguish than traditional structure fires. The Chief Public Health Office has recommended that air quality monitoring continue while the Summerside Fire Department considers the site to be an active fire scene, and out of an abundance of caution that more air quality tests be added to the perimeter around the area.

"The health and safety of our residents remains our top priority," said Cory Snow, Deputy Mayor City of Summerside. "The City will continue to work closely with provincial partners and technical experts as we assess results and plan for ongoing monitoring. We are committed to keeping residents informed and sharing information as it becomes available."

The City is developing a longer-term environmental monitoring plan for the area surrounding the Sunbank site. The plan will include ongoing air, water and soil sampling and will be reviewed with provincial environmental and public health officials to help identify and monitor any potential impacts over time.

If the fire restarts, people who are sensitive to smoke or who have respiratory conditions such as asthma or COPD may choose to limit outdoor activity if they experience irritation or symptoms. Anyone experiencing persistent breathing difficulties or other concerning symptoms should seek medical advice.

Testing of Summerside's drinking water has also been completed and confirms the water is safe to drink.

 For residents with home vegetable gardens, based on advice from national experts, a possible impact of smoke exposure from the fire is the deposition of particles on the surface of fruits and vegetables. Thorough washing of produce before consumption is recommended. For produce that cannot be easily washed, removing outer layers, such as the outer leaves of lettuce or cabbage, is also recommended. Properly washed garden produce is not expected to pose a risk to human health.

The City and Province thank residents for their patience, cooperation and understanding as response and monitoring efforts continue.

If the level of health risk changes, residents will be informed immediately. Based on all available information today, residents can continue their normal day-to-day activities while response and monitoring efforts continue.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
Ph: 867-767-9140 ext. 11092
